doc.title: Junior Mance Part II interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 18, 1999 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Japanese jazz fans, reissues and record shopping
summary: He praises the knowledge of Japanese audiences, their record stores and reissues, and his NARAS record purchases.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Gee the Japanese jazz audience is really quite well informed.

Oh man, aren’t they. They know so much about you, you think they slept under your bed. They’re writing out everything about you. They know everything. I’ll tell you, they buy more American jazz records than Americans do. A record is never taken out of print. Like the first record I ever made, “Junior,” on Verve, that’s still available on CD. The same cover, same album notes. And now it’s an import here. They imported it from Verve and then they’re exporting it back. Because I was in Tower one day and I saw it, I said oh it’s available here now. And I looked at the price on it — $23.00. Because it was an import. I said are they nuts? $23.00 yeah. But they had it on sale. In fact a lot of jazz records that are hard to find here, in Tokyo especially I like to frequent the record stores there, there’s one called Wave, W-A-V-E that’s the name of the store. They’ve got about two floors of just any jazz record you can name. You can ask the guy, “oh yeah, we have that.” And I remember one year I spent over $400 on records. Because CDs are higher there. They’re in the vicinity of about $20.00 apiece. So that’s only about 20 records I bought. But they’re all records that were out of print long ago in the States. But now they’re coming back, because I bought a lot of records through NARAS, you know the National Academy of Recording Arts and Sciences — the Grammy people. And I get them for seven bucks apiece because I’m a member, a voting member. That’s why they send us this monthly catalogue with all the new releases. And believe it or not, over half of the jazz releases they have are reissues. And when you get them they’re from Japan —
they’ve got this Japanese writing, and the covers inside. And so they are available here now, so I don’t have to buy quite as many at $20.00.
